parts.text:
40 A nucleus of carbon-10, 10
6C, decays by beta-emission to form a nucleus of boron-10, 10
5B.
For this decay process, what is the change to a nucleon and what is the change in the quark
composition of the nucleon?
change to nucleon
change in
quark composition
A
proton to neutron
down becomes up
B
proton to neutron
up becomes down
C
neutron to proton
down becomes up
D
neutron to proton
up becomes down

hints: Compare the subscripts in $^{10}_{6}C$ and $^{10}_{5}B$: the nucleon number stays at 10 but the proton number drops from 6 to 5, so decide which nucleon is lost and which is gained.
Recall the quark make-up $proton = uud$ and $neutron = udd$ and use it to see which single quark must change when a proton turns into a neutron.
Check that this is beta-plus emission with a positron emitted: the nucleon charge must decrease by $+1$, so track how the $+2/3$ $up$ charge is replaced by a $-1/3$ $down$ charge.
walkthrough: Identify the nuclei: $^{10}_{6}C$ has 6 protons and 4 neutrons, while $^{10}_{5}B$ has 5 protons and 5 neutrons, with total nucleons $A=10$ unchanged.
The proton number $Z$ decreases by 1 and the neutron number increases by 1, so one proton in the carbon nucleus has changed into a neutron. This is beta-plus decay.
State the quark model: a proton is $uud$ with charge $+1$ and a neutron is $udd$ with charge $0$.
To go from $uud$ to $udd$, one $up$ quark with charge $+2/3$ must change into a $down$ quark with charge $-1/3$, decreasing the nucleon charge by $+1$.
Therefore the change is proton to neutron with $up$ becomes $down$. This is option B.

A.explanation: The nucleon change is correct, but a proton is $uud$ and a neutron is $udd$, so a down quark cannot become an up quark in this change.

B.explanation: Proton number falls from 6 to 5 so a proton becomes a neutron, which requires one $up$ quark in $uud$ to become a $down$ quark to give $udd$.

C.explanation: A neutron to proton change would increase proton number from 6 to 7, which is beta-minus decay, not the observed $^{10}_{6}C$ to $^{10}_{5}B$ change.

D.explanation: The quark change $up$ becomes $down$ would form a neutron, but it cannot come from a neutron to proton change which needs $down$ becomes $up$.
